questionText:
Match the historic nuclear accident in List I with its location, year, and primary cause in List II:

List I:
(A) Three Mile Island
(B) Chernobyl Disaster
(C) Fukushima Daiichi Disaster
(D) Kyshtym Disaster (Mayak)

List II:
(I) Pennsylvania, USA (1979): Partial reactor core meltdown triggered by mechanical coolant valve failure and operator errors
(II) Ukraine, USSR (1986): Catastrophic steam explosion and graphite fire at RBMK reactor following unauthorized safety test
(III) Japan (2011): Magnitude 9.0 earthquake and 15-meter tsunami disabling emergency diesel generators, causing triple core meltdown
(IV) Chelyabinsk, USSR (1957): Explosion of high-level radioactive waste storage tank releasing massive strontium-90 cloud

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II

options.text: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III

detailedSolution:

questionText:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Managing marine fisheries strictly at the theoretical Maximum Sustainable Yield (MSY) frequently leads to catastrophic population collapse.
Reason (R): MSY models assume static environmental carrying capacity and ignore recruitment fluctuations, climatic shocks (El Niño), and multi-species ecological trophic interactions.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Validates both statements and confirms causal explanation.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to notice that Reason does not causally explain the Assertion.

options.text: (A) is true but (R) is false
options.mistakeAnalysis: Accepted an inaccurate Reason as factually true.

options.text: (A) is false but (R) is true
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to identify the scientific fallacy in the Assertion.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) correctly explains (A). Real ecosystems fluctuate; setting quotas at deterministic MSY leaves zero safety buffer against natural mortality spikes.
Hence Option A is correct.
Hence, option (A) is the correct choice.
